newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: European soy trade unruffled by Greenpeace protest.
newsitem.headline: European soy trade unruffled by Greenpeace protest.

text.p: European oilseed traders said on Tuesday they expected scant market impact from the latest round of protests across Europe against genetically-modified soybeans and grains by environmental group Greenpeace.
Traders said the last set of protests had prompted a few more queries from customers requesting details of material free of genetic modifications but very little had been traded.
"We a saw a little more interest but in terms of the overall market, the quantities involved were tiny," one said.
Greenpeace on Tuesday resumed its direct action against the use of gene-modified soy and grain in European foodstuffs.
Traders said there was very little gene-free soya actually available in Europe at the moment and the initial interest had waned once customers found out how expensive it would be.
"Nobody is even offering it, the premiums were so high," one trader said.

Greenpeace activists blockaded offices across Europe belonging to Nestle, Unilever and Danone in a co-ordinated campaign against the beans, developed by U.S. chemicals firm Monsanto and the grains, made by Swiss company Ciba Geigy AG.
